say.en: Give me the two regression lines and I can tell you the means and the correlation, without seeing a single data point. In this lesson: Use the properties of regression coefficients.
Find the means and r from two regression lines.

body.en: $r = \pm\sqrt{b_{yx} b_{xy}}$: r is the geometric mean of the two coefficients and takes their common sign. Both coefficients have the same sign. Since $r^2 \le 1$, if one coefficient is greater than 1 the other must be less than 1. *Regression coefficients* are independent of change of origin but not of scale. The lines meet at $(\bar{x}, \bar{y})$; they coincide when r = ±1 and are perpendicular (parallel to the axes) when r = 0.
body.kn: r = ±√(b_yx·b_xy): r ಎರಡು ಗುಣಾಂಕಗಳ ಗುಣೋತ್ತರ ಸರಾಸರಿ, ಅವುಗಳ ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಚಿಹ್ನೆ ಹೊಂದಿರುತ್ತದೆ. ಎರಡೂ ಗುಣಾಂಕಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ಚಿಹ್ನೆ. ಒಂದು 1 ಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚಾದರೆ ಇನ್ನೊಂದು 1 ಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಕಡಿಮೆ. ರೇಖೆಗಳು (x̄, ȳ) ನಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಧಿಸುತ್ತವೆ; r = ±1 ಆದರೆ ಒಂದಾಗುತ್ತವೆ, r = 0 ಆದರೆ ಲಂಬವಾಗುತ್ತವೆ.

say.en: r = \pm\sqrt{b yx b xy}: r is the geometric mean of the two coefficients and takes their common sign. Both coefficients have the same sign. Since r^2 \le 1, if one coefficient is greater than 1 the other must be less than 1. Regression coefficients are independent of change of origin but not of scale. title.en: Means and r from two lines

say.en: The lines are three x plus two y equals twenty-six, and six x plus y equals thirty-one.
Both pass through the means, so solve them together. Twice (2) minus (1) gives nine x equal to thirty-six.
Take (1) as Y on X: y is thirteen minus 1.5 x, so b y x is minus 1.5. Take (2) as X on Y: b x y is minus one sixth.
So r is minus the root of a quarter: minus 0.5. If the product had exceeded one, we would swap the roles of the lines.

problem.en: Regression lines: 3x + 2y = 26 and 6x + y = 31. Find x̄, ȳ and r.

steps.en: Solving: 2 × (2) − (1) gives 9x = 36, so x̄ = 4 and ȳ = 31 − 24 = 7.
Y on X from (1): y = 13 − 1.5x, b_yx = −1.5.
r² = 0.25 and the sign is negative: r = −0.5.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Regression lines: 3x + 2y = 26 and 6x + y = 31. Find x̄, ȳ and r.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Regression lines: 3x plus 2y equals 26 and 6x plus y equals 31. Find x̄, ȳ and r.
Solving: 2 times 2 - 1 gives 9x equals 36, so x̄ = 4 and ȳ equals 31 minus 24 equals 7.
Y on X from 1: y equals 13 minus 1.5x, b yx equals minus 1.5.
X on Y from 2: x equals 31 over 6 - y over 6, b xy equals minus 1 over 6.
r squared equals 0.25 and the sign is negative: r equals minus 0.5.
So the answer is x̄ = 4, ȳ equals 7, r equals minus 0.5.
